en.basics_01: Here at Fraction Farms, we showcase how to divide up land in order to produce crops more efficiently.
en.basics_02: We do this by taking Unit Tiles and breaking their sides into fractional lengths.
en.basics_03: For each side, there is a back and forward button to increase and decrease the number of parts each side is divided up into.
en.basics_04: We can select each individual piece to count up the number of fractional tiles that intersect with the portion of the area we are looking to use.
en.basics_05: Once you have selected the right number of tiles, you can click the submit button to check your results.
en.basics_08: You're a fast learner! Great job!
en.basics_09: Notice how the solution we are getting is the same as if we multiplied the fractions together, multiplying the numerators togehter and the denominators together.
en.basics_11: Wonderful! You've mastered working with one tile, but dividing up land sometimes takes multiple tiles.
en.basics_12: Let's move onto another part of the farm!
en.mixed_01: We need more than one tile when were dealing with numbers greater than one.
en.mixed_02: Working with multiple tiles is easy, though. You just need to click on the tile you want to interact with to enable it.
en.mixed_03: We can still count up the tiles, but because we are dealing with mixed tiles of fractional size, we show the answer with the common denominator.
en.mixed_05: Great job! Notice how the same rule applies, that we get the same solution had we multiplied the two numbers together.
en.mixed_07: Good job! Keep it up! You're doing great!
en.mixed_09: I'm impressed! You've done really well to come this far.
en.mixed_10: You know, there is another way we can look at these problems that reference back to when we used one tile. Come on, I'll show you!
en.improper_01: Another way we can visualize using multiple tiles is by slicing up all the tiles by the same denominators, and counting the individual tiles up together.
en.improper_02: This will require us to look at our fractions as improper fractions. Let's take the problem we just completed and do it again, but looking at it as improper fractions.
en.improper_03: Well done! Now, on your own, convert the problem to improper fractions and solve the next problems using this method.
en.improper_04: Nicely done! Let's try the next one!
en.improper_05: Excellent! Just one more to go.
en.improper_06: Bravo! You've become quite the expert at being able to divide up land.
en.improper_07: I think you're ready to try dividing up not just the land, but manage multiple crops that we need to produce. Let's go to the last land plot!
